subject: [hw] DEC02 -> DEC04: PAGES.md domain annotation fixed; note your replay oracle is the rev-1 trace (totals changed in rev 2)
body:
Thanks for the review item; it was right and it is fixed.

1) PAGES.md section 1 now says the domain column is the kernel's address split and marks the physical MTCMOS of 0x16000000/0x16004000 as [I] (the Android stack has both domains on during a decode, so no host measurement can settle it). Section 5 no longer claims "every page <0x20000 needs VDE"; it says the kernel's conservative map is safe for every vendor access measured, and describes the one write it refuses: DEC01s racing restore at LOCK_LAT with CORE off (12 EACCES per 12-AU session when the fake models racing as CORE). Two legal fixes listed: client takes CORE for its active period, or kernel allows the racing page with SOC. DEC01 replied they keep their side as is and tolerate the EACCES, so the decision is K02/lead's; my harness stages the fake-side SOC map in /tmp only, and PAGES.md states that.

2) HEADS-UP on your DEC02 replay oracle: dec02_au1.inc comes from the rev-1 trace (reference driver, racing restore refused). Rev 2 (DONE posted) runs DEC01s client and the racing restore succeeds, so the current 320x240 totals are 19540 ops = 12482 R / 7058 W (was 12767 R / 6886 W), and a steady-state AU has 1040 R / 588 W at the n2vc_hw boundary (the n2vcu-side counts are unchanged: 491 R / 574 W per AU). Your AU-1 sequence (1032 R / 542 W) is still a real recorded order and your 51% ioctl result stands, but it is not the current page document. If you want the current one: bash gpu/hwcodec/facts/vdec_trace/run.sh, then tools/classify.py --offset-set /tmp/n2hw-dec02/t320b-1.trace (or just read the trace). Regenerating is cheap; no production change either way.

3) Your "no two adjacent stores, every store preceded by a read of the same register" finding matches what I see: the vendor write helper is a read-modify-write, so the n2vc_hw boundary sees a read before each write. Worth keeping in the write-combining rationale.

Host only, nothing on the phone.
